title: TimesNet: Temporal 2D-Variation Modeling for General Time Series Analysis
grouping: Three stages without containers: an axis plot of the raw series at the left with nested brackets 'Period 1/2/3' above it; dashed arrows from each bracket to a diagonal staircase of period stacks in the middle; hollow block arrows to three slanted 2-D planes at the right. A legend in the lower-left explains the circles and the two arrow colours.
shapes_depth: The series is a grey line on a Value/Time axis. In the middle each period's segments are drawn as offset copies of the grey curve on alternating pale blue and pale pink rectangles; black hollow circles mark time points at the same phase and dashed lines join them across copies. Dark blue arrows trace the interperiod variation along a copy, dark red curved arrows the intraperiod variation across copies. The right-hand 2-D planes are white parallelograms in perspective containing short black curve fragments, with a long blue arrow along one edge and a red arrow along the other; finer periods give more, narrower cells.
proposed_highlight: The paper's key idea (two kinds of variation) owns the only two saturated colours, blue and red, used identically on the curve overlays, the 2-D planes' axes and the legend.
lesson: Explain a 1-D-to-2-D reshape by cutting the drawn series into period segments stacked as offset copies with same-phase points joined, and give the two resulting axes their own colours (blue across periods, red within) on both the curves and the final 2-D planes.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF header (Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023). Annotation note (2026-11-15): Conceptual motivation figure (1D-to-2D multi-periodicity), not the network architecture figure.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: architecture = reshaping a 1D series into 2D tensors by period (multi-periodicity), shown conceptually

insights.structure: Three columns left to right: a single value-time plot with three nested period spans, a middle column of three stacked series segmentations (Period 1/2/3), and right three slanted 2D planes of decreasing period length.
insights.data: Series are grey jagged line plots; same-phase time points are hollow circles joined by dashed lines; segments are tinted blue (interperiod) and red (intraperiod) bands; 2D tensors are drawn as skewed parallelograms holding short squiggles.
insights.emphasis: Two colours carry the whole idea: blue arrows for interperiod variation along rows and red arrows for intraperiod variation along columns, repeated on each 2D plane and in the bottom-left legend.
insights.flow: Long black dashed arrows fan from each period span on the left plot to its segmented copy in the middle, then hollow block arrows point right to the 2D plane.
insights.avoid: The middle column's overlapping, offset series copies with dashed connectors and circles are very busy and partly illegible.

arrangement.units: unframed three-column progression (1D plot, per-period segments, 2D planes)
arrangement.inputs_as: a plotted 1D time series with period spans marked
